intro: Searching for cosmetic surgery near me usually means you're thinking seriously about changing something about your appearance and want to talk it through with a surgeon you can actually get to. You may have a particular operation in mind, or you may still be working out what's right for you. Either way, the first step is a proper consultation with the surgeon who would carry out the procedure.
need_heading: What people searching for cosmetic surgery near me usually need
need_lead: Most people at this stage want a local, reputable surgeon and a clear picture of what a consultation involves before committing to anything.
needs: You have a specific operation in mind, such as breast surgery, eyelid surgery, a facelift or body contouring, and want to discuss it face to face with a surgeon.
You would prefer a clinic or hospital within reasonable travelling distance, especially with recovery and follow-up appointments in mind.
You want to know that the surgeon you see is on the GMC's specialist register and that the place you're treated is registered with the CQC, or the equivalent regulator outside England.
You have questions about recovery, time away from work and aftercare, and want honest answers before deciding anything.
You feel ready to take the next step but want time to reflect afterwards rather than being pushed towards a decision.
context_heading: Who should carry out your cosmetic surgery
context: Cosmetic surgery should be carried out by a surgeon on the GMC's specialist register, usually in plastic surgery or a related specialty, working in a hospital or clinic registered with the CQC, or the equivalent regulator outside England. Many surgeons are members of BAAPS or BAPRAS, and the Royal College of Surgeons offers a cosmetic surgery certification. These are useful things to check when you look into a surgeon near you.

The GMC requires doctors offering cosmetic interventions to give you time to reflect before agreeing to surgery and not to use high-pressure sales. Your consultation should be with the surgeon who will actually operate, so ask about this when you make contact.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say which operation you are considering, or describe the change you are hoping for if you are not sure of the name.
Mention the area you live in and how far you are willing to travel for consultations and follow-up appointments.
Explain whether you have already seen a surgeon or had a consultation elsewhere, so we understand where you are starting from.
Note any particular concerns you want to raise, such as recovery time or aftercare arrangements.
Say whether you would prefer a particular type of setting, such as a hospital or clinic, if that matters to you.
Include the best way to reach you so a suitable professional can respond with a quote.
questions: Are you on the GMC's specialist register, and in which specialty?
Is the hospital or clinic where you operate registered with the CQC, or the equivalent regulator outside England?
Will my consultation be with you, the surgeon who would carry out the operation?
How much time will I have to reflect before deciding whether to go ahead?
What does recovery involve for this operation, and what aftercare will you provide?
What is included in your quote, and are there costs that would only become clear later?

faqs.q: How do I check a cosmetic surgeon near me is properly qualified?
faqs.a: You can check whether a surgeon is on the GMC's specialist register, usually in plastic surgery or a related specialty. It is also worth confirming that the hospital or clinic is registered with the CQC, or the equivalent regulator outside England.

faqs.q: Will I be pressured to book surgery at my first appointment?
faqs.a: The GMC requires doctors offering cosmetic interventions to give you time to reflect before agreeing to surgery and not to use high-pressure sales. You should feel free to take that time and ask questions.

faqs.q: Should my consultation be with the surgeon who will operate?
faqs.a: Yes. The GMC's guidance is that your consultation should be with the surgeon who will carry out the operation, so ask about this when you make contact.

faqs.q: How does iComply help me find a cosmetic surgeon near me?
faqs.a: You tell us what you need and where you are, and we introduce you to a suitable UK professional who quotes you directly. We do not provide the surgery or give professional advice ourselves.
